subject: When someone you trusted turns on you
preview: Joseph's story starts in a pit. It does not end there.
linkText: Who Was Joseph? From the Pit to the Palace

blocks.text: Somebody you trusted turned on you.
A door you did not deserve got slammed shut anyway.
And now you are sitting in a season that makes no sense, wondering if God even sees it.
That is exactly where Joseph's story starts.
A favorite son, thrown in a pit by his own brothers.
Sold for twenty pieces of silver.
Falsely accused. Thrown in prison. Forgotten by the one man who could have spoken up for him.
Thirteen years passed between the pit and the palace.
But Scripture keeps repeating one line, on purpose.
"And the LORD was with Joseph."
In a slave owner's house. In a prison cell. Before anything got better.
God's presence was never a reward for Joseph's circumstances improving. It was the constant underneath every one of them.
And the ending is not the one you would expect.
Judah, the brother who suggested selling Joseph, later offers himself as a slave to save his youngest brother.
Then Joseph looks his betrayers in the face and chooses forgiveness instead of revenge.
Listen to what he tells them.
"But as for you, ye thought evil against me; but God meant it unto good, to bring to pass, as it is this day, to save much people alive."
He does not pretend the evil never happened.
He holds both things at once. What you did was evil. And God used it for good.
You may not be in a pit or a prison. But the season you are in is not empty either.
In the full guide I walk through the whole story in order, from the dreams to the palace, with five lessons from Joseph's life.
